신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
주제찾기
1 1번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
For centuries, English has served as a world language. It traveled mainly with people who moved from Britain to lands like Australia, New Zealand, and North America. In places such as India, Nigeria, and the Philippines, colonial rule also helped it spread. Today there are so many varieties of English that nobody can count them, and each has its own features because a language changes to meet the different needs of the people who use it. All these varieties together make up what we now call "World Englishes." The term covers not only the English of Britain and the United States, where most people speak it as a first language, but also that of India, Singapore, and Kenya, where it is an official language. It even includes the English of the Expanding Circle, a group of countries described by Braj Kachru. In Korea, Mexico, and China, for example, English is learned mainly as a foreign language for international communication. There, people whose mother tongues differ often turn to English to talk with one another.
①why English is the easiest language for foreigners to learn
②how English spread and developed into the many varieties called World Englishes
③the negative effects of colonial rule on local languages
④the need for one fixed standard of English pronunciation
⑤the number of English learners in each Expanding Circle country
2 2번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The term British English is used for the different forms of English found in the United Kingdom. Most people who imagine the "standard" sound of British English have Received Pronunciation, or RP, in mind. RP is the best-known accent in the country, mainly because it is heard so often in the media and is used by famous people like the King. Yet the UK is also home to Welsh English, Scots English, and Hiberno-English. Each of these has been strongly shaped by the local languages of its region, so even British people sometimes struggle to understand one another. In Scots English, for example, Dinnae ken means "I don't know," and Aye, a wee bit means "Yes, a little bit." In Northern England, the Vikings left words that are still used today, such as fell for "hill" and bairn for "child."
①the reasons RP is losing popularity
②how the Vikings conquered Northern England
③tips for learning a Scottish accent
④the variety of English spoken within the United Kingdom
⑤the role of the King in protecting the English language
1
신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
주제찾기
3 3번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The varieties of English used in the United States and Canada are together known as American English. English arrived there with the British in the 16th century, and since then both countries have become melting pots shaped by languages from every corner of the world. Newcomers from many lands carried their own tongues with them, and these languages helped form the standard American English we know today. American English is frequently compared with British English, and the two differ in vocabulary, pronunciation, and spelling. What Americans call a parking lot, for instance, is known as a car park in Britain. Americans also pronounce the "r" in words such as car, hard, and market, while the British usually leave it silent. In spelling, American English prefers "z" where British English often uses "s," as in realize and realise.
①American English: its origins and how it differs from British English
②why British English is more correct than American English
③the history of immigration laws in Canada
④how to improve your English spelling
⑤the disappearance of the letter "r" from English
4 4번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
English reached Australia in the 18th century, and Australian English borrows features from both British and American English. Still, it has plenty of characteristics that belong to it alone. The first British settlers met plants and animals they had never seen before, so they needed new words such as koala and kangaroo to describe them. Over the years, the variety has kept changing, and today it contains many expressions found only in Australia. Australians say hoo-roo when they leave, much as the British say cheerio. Because Australians enjoy making things shorter, some of their expressions can confuse outsiders. One of them is "Yeah, nah": Australians see no reason to say "Yes, I understand you, but I still disagree" when two short words will do.
①the history of British settlement in North America
②why Australians dislike British English
③the animals that live only in Australia
④how to say goodbye politely in English
⑤the distinct features of Australian English and where they came from

신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
주제찾기
5 5번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The varieties of English found in countries such as India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka are called South Asian English. The language first came to the Indian subcontinent in the early 17th century, and long years of British rule made its place even stronger. Even today, some countries in the region use English as an official language. India, for example, did not give up English after gaining independence, because it has hundreds of native languages besides Hindi. With roughly 125 million speakers, Indian English is the best-known South Asian variety, and it is sometimes called "Hinglish," a blend of Hindi and English. Speakers often add English words to Hindi, but the meanings of those words can shift as time passes. In Indian English, would-be refers to the person someone is going to marry, and airdash means to travel somewhere quickly by plane.
①the decline of Hindi in modern India
②why English became the only language of India
③the history and features of English in South Asia
④wedding customs in South Asia
⑤how air travel changed life in India
6 6번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
The term African English could mean English used anywhere in Africa, but it usually refers to the English of Sub-Saharan Africa. Today, English is an official language in 27 countries on the continent. One major variety is South African English, which has been official in South Africa ever since the British arrived in 1795. The many languages spoken in the country have strongly shaped the English used there. As a result, South African English has some colorful words and phrases. People may greet each other by saying Howzit! instead of asking how things are going, traffic lights are known as robots, and lekker means "nice." Visitors are often puzzled when a South African promises, "I'll do it just now." The phrase does not promise immediate action; it only means the task might be done at some point later.
①the features of African English, especially South African English
②the history of British colonies in Asia
③why traffic rules differ around the world
④the number of languages spoken in Africa
⑤how to make friends in South Africa

7 7번 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
Throughout this unit, we have seen that English has traveled farther around the world than any other language. Along the way, it has become the main tool people use to communicate across borders and cultures. This spread has produced a huge number of English varieties, which we now call World Englishes. From British and American English to Australian, South Asian, and African English, each variety reflects the needs of the people who speak it. English is therefore not owned only by those who learned it as their first language. It equally belongs to the many people around the world who use it as a second or foreign language. In this sense, English has truly become everyone's language.

②why some English varieties are disappearing

It even includes the English of the Expanding Circle, a group of countries described by Braj Kachru. In Korea, Mexico, and China, for example, English is learned mainly as a foreign language for international communication. There, people whose mother tongues differ often turn to English to talk with one another.
①A language adapts to the way of life of the community that speaks it.
②A language becomes simpler as more people learn it.
③People must change their needs to fit the language they speak.
④Only native speakers can decide how a language develops.
⑤A language loses its features when it travels abroad.
23 2번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
The term British English is used for the different forms of English found in the United Kingdom. Most people who imagine the "standard" sound of British English have Received Pronunciation, or RP, in mind. RP is the best-known accent in the country, mainly because it is heard so often in the media and is used by famous people like the King. Yet the UK is also home to Welsh English, Scots English, and Hiberno-English. Each of these has been strongly shaped by the local languages of its region, so even British people sometimes struggle to understand one another. In Scots English, for example, Dinnae ken means "I don't know," and Aye, a wee bit means "Yes, a little bit." In Northern England, the Vikings left words that are still used today, such as fell for "hill" and bairn for "child."
①British people are not interested in talking with each other.
②Most British people cannot speak RP correctly.
③Regional varieties within the UK can differ greatly from one another.
④Foreign tourists make communication in the UK difficult.
⑤The British media uses too many difficult words.

신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
함축의미
24 3번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
The varieties of English used in the United States and Canada are together known as American English. English arrived there with the British in the 16th century, and since then both countries have become melting pots shaped by languages from every corner of the world. Newcomers from many lands carried their own tongues with them, and these languages helped form the standard American English we know today. American English is frequently compared with British English, and the two differ in vocabulary, pronunciation, and spelling. What Americans call a parking lot, for instance, is known as a car park in Britain. Americans also pronounce the "r" in words such as car, hard, and market, while the British usually leave it silent. In spelling, American English prefers "z" where British English often uses "s," as in realize and realise.
①The two countries became famous for their cooking.
②Immigrants gave up their languages as soon as they arrived.
③The two countries were divided by many language conflicts.
④English in North America stayed exactly the same as in Britain.
⑤Many different languages blended together to shape the English of these countries.
25 4번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
English reached Australia in the 18th century, and Australian English borrows features from both British and American English. Still, it has plenty of characteristics that belong to it alone. The first British settlers met plants and animals they had never seen before, so they needed new words such as koala and kangaroo to describe them. Over the years, the variety has kept changing, and today it contains many expressions found only in Australia. Australians say hoo-roo when they leave, much as the British say cheerio. Because Australians enjoy making things shorter, some of their expressions can confuse outsiders. One of them is "Yeah, nah": Australians see no reason to say "Yes, I understand you, but I still disagree" when two short words will do.
①Australians use only two words in every conversation.
②Short words are more polite than long ones.
③Foreigners should learn just two Australian words.
④A short expression can carry the meaning of a whole sentence.
⑤Australians do not like talking with strangers.

26 5번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
The varieties of English found in countries such as India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka are called South Asian English. The language first came to the Indian subcontinent in the early 17th century, and long years of British rule made its place even stronger. Even today, some countries in the region use English as an official language. India, for example, did not give up English after gaining independence, because it has hundreds of native languages besides Hindi. With roughly 125 million speakers, Indian English is the best-known South Asian variety, and it is sometimes called "Hinglish," a blend of Hindi and English. Speakers often add English words to Hindi, but the meanings of those words can shift as time passes. In Indian English, would-be refers to the person someone is going to marry, and airdash means to travel somewhere quickly by plane.
①Hindi words are slowly disappearing from Indian English.
②English words used in India can come to mean something different from the original.
③Indians change their spoken language every few years.
④The spelling of English words becomes simpler over time.
⑤Older speakers cannot understand English at all.
27 6번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
The term African English could mean English used anywhere in Africa, but it usually refers to the English of Sub-Saharan Africa. Today, English is an official language in 27 countries on the continent. One major variety is South African English, which has been official in South Africa ever since the British arrived in 1795. The many languages spoken in the country have strongly shaped the English used there. As a result, South African English has some colorful words and phrases. People may greet each other by saying Howzit! instead of asking how things are going, traffic lights are known as robots, and lekker means "nice." Visitors are often puzzled when a South African promises, "I'll do it just now." The phrase does not promise immediate action; it only means the task might be done at some point later.
①words that describe the colors of the national flag
②phrases that are printed in many different colors
③words borrowed only from British English
④words and phrases that are lively and unusual, shaped by local languages
⑤phrases that are too difficult to pronounce

28 7번 밑줄 친 부분이 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
Throughout this unit, we have seen that English has traveled farther around the world than any other language. Along the way, it has become the main tool people use to communicate across borders and cultures. This spread has produced a huge number of English varieties, which we now call World Englishes. From British and American English to Australian, South Asian, and African English, each variety reflects the needs of the people who speak it. English is therefore not owned only by those who learned it as their first language. It equally belongs to the many people around the world who use it as a second or foreign language. In this sense, English has truly become everyone's language.

People may greet each other by saying Howzit! instead of asking how things are going, traffic lights are known as robots, and lekker means "nice." Visitors are often puzzled when a South African promises, "I'll do it just now." The phrase does not promise immediate action; .

For centuries, English has served as a world language. It traveled mainly with people who moved from Britain to lands like Australia, New Zealand, and North America. In places such as India, Nigeria, and the Philippines, colonial rule also helped it spread. Today there are so many varieties of English that nobody can count them, and each has its own features because a language changes to meet the different needs of the people who use it. All these varieties together make up what we now call "World Englishes." The term covers not only the English of Britain and the United States, where most people speak it as a first language, but also that of India, Singapore, and Kenya, where it is an official language. It even includes the English of the Expanding Circle, a group of countries described by Braj Kachru. In Korea, Mexico, and China, for example, English is learned mainly as a foreign language for international communication. There, people whose mother tongues differ often turn to English to talk with one another.

The term British English is used for the different forms of English found in the United Kingdom. Most people who imagine the "standard" sound of British English have Received Pronunciation, or RP, in mind. RP is the best-known accent in the country, mainly because it is heard so often in the media and is used by famous people like the King. Yet the UK is also home to Welsh English, Scots English, and Hiberno-English. Each of these has been strongly shaped by the local languages of its region, so even British people sometimes struggle to understand one another. In Scots English, for example, Dinnae ken means "I don't know," and Aye, a wee bit means "Yes, a little bit." In Northern England, the Vikings left words that are still used today, such as fell for "hill" and bairn for "child."
Besides the well-known accent called RP, the UK has many (A) varieties of English, which have been shaped by the languages of their (B) regions.

English arrived there with the British in the 16th century, and since then both countries have become melting pots shaped by languages from every corner of the world. Newcomers from many lands carried their own tongues with them, and these languages helped form the standard American English we know today. American English is frequently compared with British English, and the two differ in vocabulary, pronunciation, and spelling. What Americans call a parking lot, for instance, is known as a car park in Britain. Americans also pronounce the "r" in words such as car, hard, and market, while the British usually leave it silent. In spelling, American English prefers "z" where British English often uses "s," as in realize and realise.

English reached Australia in the 18th century, and Australian English borrows features from both British and American English. Still, it has plenty of characteristics that belong to it alone. The first British settlers met plants and animals they had never seen before, so they needed new words such as koala and kangaroo to describe them. Over the years, the variety has kept changing, and today it contains many expressions found only in Australia. Australians say hoo-roo when they leave, much as the British say cheerio. Because Australians enjoy making things shorter, some of their expressions can confuse outsiders. One of them is "Yeah, nah": Australians see no reason to say "Yes, I understand you, but I still disagree" when two short words will do.

The varieties of English found in countries such as India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka are called South Asian English. The language first came to the Indian subcontinent in the early 17th century, and long years of British rule made its place even stronger. Even today, some countries in the region use English as an official language. India, for example, did not give up English after gaining independence, because it has hundreds of native languages besides Hindi. With roughly 125 million speakers, Indian English is the best-known South Asian variety, and it is sometimes called "Hinglish," a blend of Hindi and English. Speakers often add English words to Hindi, but the meanings of those words can shift as time passes. In Indian English, would-be refers to the person someone is going to marry, and airdash means to travel somewhere quickly by plane.

신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
요약문
77 7번 다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Throughout this unit, we have seen that English has traveled farther around the world than any other language. Along the way, it has become the main tool people use to communicate across borders and cultures. This spread has produced a huge number of English varieties, which we now call World Englishes. From British and American English to Australian, South Asian, and African English, each variety reflects the needs of the people who speak it. English is therefore not owned only by those who learned it as their first language. It equally belongs to the many people around the world who use it as a second or foreign language. In this sense, English has truly become everyone's language.
Having spread more (A) than any other language, English has produced World Englishes and now belongs to both its native and (B) users.
(A)(B)
①extensivelynon-native
②extensivelyancient
③slowlynon-native
④slowlyancient
⑤rarelyroyal

신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
서술형 (본문 제시) · 1번
English has been a global language for centuries. English mostly spread by migration from Britain to places such as Australia, New Zealand, and North America. Colonialism also played a role in countries including India, Nigeria, and the Philippines. Nowadays, the varieties of English are countless, and they have their own characteristics since languages evolve to fulfill the diverse needs of the societies that use them. The multiple varieties of English thus developed have given rise to "World Englishes." World Englishes include not just the varieties of English spoken in countries like Britain and the United States where English is the first language of most people. They also include the varieties used in nations such as India, Singapore, and Kenya, in which English is an official language in education, business, and government. Additionally, the term "World Englishes" covers varieties spoken in the Expanding Circle as described by Braj Kachru. They include English varieties spoken in countries like Korea, Mexico, and China, where English is used primarily as a foreign language for international communication. In these Expanding Circle countries, English is often used for communication between speakers whose native languages are different. Let's explore some of the most prominent World Englishes.
78 1번 요약문 완성
본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
English has developed into (A) varieties, and in Expanding Circle countries it is used as a (B) language for international communication.
45
신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
서술형 (본문 제시) · 2번
British English refers to the varieties that exist in the United Kingdom (UK). When you think of how "standard" British English sounds, you are probably thinking of Received Pronunciation (RP). RP is the most well-known British accent because of its prominence in the media and its usage by famous figures, such as the King. Variants of English in the UK include Welsh English, Scots English, and Hiberno-English. These varieties have been heavily influenced by the languages spoken in their respective regions, resulting in a situation in which even British individuals sometimes find it hard to understand each other. Take the Scots English phrases Dinnae ken, and Aye, a wee bit, for instance. Did you know they mean, "I don't know," and "Yes, a little bit," respectively? In Northern England, the Vikings have left a lasting impact, with words like fell meaning "hill" and bairn meaning "child."
79 2번 요약문 완성
본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
Regional varieties in the UK are so different that even British people sometimes find it (A) to understand each other, and some words, like fell and bairn, show the (B) impact of the Vikings.
46
신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
서술형 (본문 제시) · 3번
American English is the name given to the varieties spoken in the United States of America (USA) and Canada. Since the 16th century, when the British brought the English language with them, the USA and Canada have become melting pots with linguistic influences from all over the globe. People from around the world brought their own languages with them. These have influenced standard American English as we know it today. American English is often contrasted with British English, and many differences between the two are noted in vocabulary, pronunciation, and spelling. For example, a parking lot in American English is called a car park in British English. In pronunciation, the letter "r" is pronounced in words like car, hard, or market in American English, whereas it remains silent in British English. Also, American English tends to use the letter "z" rather than the letter "s," which is common in British English, as in realize vs. realise.

American English became a mix of many (A) influences, and it is different from British English in vocabulary, pronunciation, and (B).
47
신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
서술형 (본문 제시) · 4번
English came to Australia in the 18th century. Australian English uses features from both British and American English. However, Australian English does have many of its own distinct features. When British settlers first arrived, many new words had to be created to describe the unique plants and animals in Australia, such as koala and kangaroo. Australian English has evolved over time and now includes many words and phrases unique to the country. Comparable to the British cheerio, hoo-roo is used by Australians to say goodbye. Some phrases may be puzzling since Australians love to shorten things. An example is the phrase, "Yeah, nah." This phrase is confusing, but Australians think: why bother saying, "Yes, I understand you, but still disagree," when you could simply say, "Yeah, nah"?
81 4번 요약문 완성
본문을 한 문장으로 요약할 때 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
Australian English has many (A) features of its own, and some of its phrases may be (B) to outsiders because Australians love to shorten things.
48
신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
서술형 (본문 제시) · 5번
South Asian English refers to the varieties used in countries including India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. English was introduced to the Indian subcontinent in the early 17th century and reinforced by long-term British rule. English is still used as an official language in some of the countries in the region. For example, India has kept English as an official language even after it became independent since the country has hundreds of native languages aside from Hindi. The most popular variety of South Asian English is Indian English with about 125 million speakers. It is sometimes called "Hinglish," a mix of Hindi and English. Indian English typically adds English words to Hindi; however, the meanings can change over time. For instance, would-be in Indian English means "a fiancé" or "a fiancée," while airdash is the word for "travel hastily by plane."

English was brought to the Indian subcontinent and is still used as an (A) language there, and Indian English, or Hinglish, is a (B) of Hindi and English.

신목고 2-2 기말 · 세계문화
서술형 (본문 제시) · 6번
While African English can refer to English spoken anywhere within Africa, the term is typically reserved for Sub-Saharan Africa. Today, 27 countries on the continent recognize English as an official language. South African English is a major variety of African English. English has been an official language in South Africa since the British arrived in 1795. Many languages present in the nation have dramatically influenced the variety of English used there. For one, South African English has some colorful words and phrases. For instance, when they meet someone, they might say Howzit! instead of "Hello, how's it going?" Traffic lights in South Africa are called robots, and lekker means "nice." English speakers from other countries are sometimes confused when a South African says, "I'll do it just now." That does not mean that they will do it now. It actually means they might do it sometime in the future.

The process has given rise to countless varieties of English, known as World Englishes. The English language belongs not only to its native speakers but also to its diverse non-native users worldwide. It truly has become a language for everyone!

1 1번 주제찾기 정답 ②
해설: 영어가 이주와 식민 지배로 퍼지고, 사회의 필요에 맞게 변하며 세계 영어라는 수많은 변종을 낳았다는 내용이므로 ②가 주제이다.

해설: 확산을 말한 주어진 문장 뒤에 (A) The process 가 그 확산이 낳은 세계 영어를 받고, (C) 영어가 모든 사용자의 것이라는 주장, (B) It 으로 그 결론을 감탄문으로 맺으므로 ③이다.
(A)의 The process 는 주어진 문장의 확산을 바로 받아야 하고, (B)의 It … for everyone 은 (C)의 원어민·비원어민을 아우른 뒤에야 결론이 된다.
64 1번 문장삽입 정답 ②
해설: 주어진 문장의 also 는 앞에서 말한 이주(migration)에 이어 또 하나의 확산 경로를 덧붙이므로, 이주를 설명한 문장 뒤인 ②에 들어가야 한다.
① 자리에서는 아직 확산 경로가 하나도 나오지 않아 also 가 받을 말이 없고, ③ 이후는 이미 확산이 끝나고 변종의 특징과 세계 영어로 넘어간 뒤다.

해설: 주어진 문장의 they 는 두 개의 표현을 가리키고 respectively 로 순서대로 뜻을 짝지으므로, Dinnae ken 과 Aye, a wee bit 가 처음 나온 문장 뒤인 ⑤에 들어가야 한다.
①~④ 자리에는 they 가 가리킬 두 표현이 아직 나오지 않아 respectively 가 짝지을 대상이 없다.
66 3번 문장삽입 정답 ③

①② 자리에는 These 가 가리킬 언어들이 아직 나오지 않았고, ④⑤ 이후는 이미 영국 영어와의 비교로 넘어간 뒤다.

① 자리에는 아직 영어가 도입되기 전이고, ③ 이후는 예시와 인도 영어 소개로 넘어간 뒤라 일반 진술이 들어갈 자리가 아니다.

①②③ 자리에는 That 이 가리킬 "just now"가 아직 나오지 않았고, ⑤ 자리는 actually 로 정정한 뒤라 부정이 너무 늦게 나온다.

② 이후에 넣으면 these varieties 가 가리킬 변종이 앞에 없게 되고, The process 가 받을 확산 과정과도 멀어진다.
71 1번 요약문 정답 ⑤
해설: 영어는 사회의 필요에 맞춰 변하며(evolved) 수많은 변종이 되었고, 세계 영어는 모국어·공용어·외국어 사용자, 즉 원어민과 비원어민(non-native)의 영어를 모두 포함하므로 ⑤이다.
shrunk·disappeared 는 변종이 셀 수 없이 많아졌다는 내용과 반대이고, British 는 원어민 쪽에 속하며 young 은 근거가 없다.
72 2번 요약문 정답 ①
해설: RP 외에 지역마다 다른(regional) 변종들이 있고, 그것들은 각자(respective) 지역의 언어에 영향을 받았으므로 ①이다.
identical 은 서로 알아듣기 어려울 만큼 다르다는 내용과 반대이고, foreign 은 외국이 아니라 각 지역의 언어라는 점에서 틀리며, modern·northern 은 근거가 없거나 범위가 좁다.
73 3번 요약문 정답 ②

confused·replaced 는 본문의 "대조된다"와 다르고, grammar·history 는 차이의 영역으로 제시되지 않았다.
74 4번 요약문 정답 ③
해설: 호주 영어는 고유한(distinct) 단어와 어구를 발전시켰고, 호주 사람들은 말을 줄이길(shorten) 좋아한다고 했으므로 ③이다.
borrowed 는 고유 표현을 발전시켰다는 내용과 반대이고, repeat·explain 은 "Yeah, nah"처럼 짧게 줄이는 습관과 반대이며, formal 은 근거가 없다.
75 5번 요약문 정답 ④

tourism·music 은 영어가 들어온 경로로 제시되지 않았고, sounds·spellings 는 본문이 말한 의미 변화와 다르다.
